prior_year_events.event_name: Reinsurance to Close of 2014 year (including 2007 of Syndicate 1208 and 2011 of Syndicate 102)
prior_year_events.impact_description: Acceptance of the RITC transferred legacy years (including 2007 and 2011 books) into the syndicate, adding legacy reserves and affecting comparability of claims development and reserves.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate's gross claims outstanding decreased modestly from GBP 14.059m at the opening balance to GBP 11.701m at year end, with prior-year development implying an overall small release of approximately GBP 0.99m. The claims development triangle shows favourable development in the 2011 underwriting year more than offsetting a small adverse movement in 2012. Interpretation is complicated by RITC activity bringing legacy years into the syndicate and by historical volatility in the liability book.
raw_causal_phrases: the continuing assessment of the reserving position due to historic volatility experienced in the liability book.

The most uncertain element within these technical provisions is the amount for claims outstanding which covers amounts where either the claim has been notified to the syndicate or where there has not yet been a notification or although notified there has been insufficient information to date to be certain regarding its ultimate costs.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development computed from the gross claims development triangle (pages 26-27). Triangle covers only two underwriting years (2011 and 2012) and RITC activity (acceptance of 2014 RITC into 2017) may distort comparability; no explicit sentence quantifying gross prior-year movement was found. Amounts in reports are presented in GBP 000; conversions to millions performed by dividing by 1,000. Prior-year development therefore has moderate confidence.
